title: Environment root marker
description: `<root>/.claude/exchange.json`. Its presence is what makes a directory a root; its contents are the config that used to be hardcoded in four scripts. Written by `exchange init`, edited by hand thereafter, and never travels with the plugin - this file is the whole reason the plugin can name no paths.

name.description: Display name for this root, used in injected context so a session can tell which exchange it is looking at.

stale_days.description: A claim or handoff older than this is flagged rather than hidden. A row that reads as current and is ten days old is worse than no row.

max_focus_chars.description: Width cap for a one-line render of text another session wrote: a claim's focus, and a handoff's scope, sender and body preview. Anything past it is counted, never silently cut. The ledger this replaces had single rows of 23 KB injected into every session. The key keeps its original name, which says focus, because renaming it would break every marker already written.

max_hot_paths.description: How many entries of each claimed list - repos, paths, tickets - to render per session. Anything beyond the cap is counted, never silently dropped. The key keeps its original name because renaming it would break every marker already written.

max_handoffs_listed.description: How many matching handoffs to render. Anything beyond the cap is counted, never silently dropped.

labels.description: Optional display-only grouping: root-relative directory to human-readable label. Never a matching key. A hand-typed label having to agree with a hand-typed label elsewhere is the defect class this design removes, so nothing is ever addressed or matched by these.

legacy_ledger.description: The markdown ledger this root's handoffs used to live in, for migration step 4 to import from. Absent means there never was one, so step 4 is not applicable here rather than outstanding (#38). `init` never writes it, so a root that did keep a ledger has to have it added. Declared rather than derived because the plugin never names a ledger path of its own: whether a root had one is a fact only its owner knows.

path.description: The ledger file. Absolute, or relative to the root.

section.description: The heading the handoffs sit under. Defaults to `Open questions / handoffs`, the heading the legacy hook read.

routes.description: Ledger recipient label to the scope its handoffs are addressed to. Labels compare case-folded and with the spacing around `/`, `&` and `+` ignored. An entry with several recipients needs every label to map to the same scope, or the whole recipient side mapped as one key, such as `Lane B + Lane C`. An entry whose recipient has no route stops the import before anything is written, because the ledger names lanes and the store addresses scopes, and only the owner knows which is which.
